purpose: Candidate alignment only; manually checked expert answers override these rules.

rules.assessment: The implemented numerator counts keyword-matching 10-K documents and the denominator counts 10-K filings. Documents can discuss risk or plans without adoption, and a document rate is not a unique-company deployment rate.

Paid cloud includes ordinary email, office software and storage. Therefore its use measures access to rented digital services, not the amount of AI work performed; comparing it with AI use does not identify an adoption gap.

A survey prevalence numerator is defined over eligible enterprises, not tasks or individuals. Matched size, sector, reference year and question wording are required; use frequency or intensity cannot be recovered from a yes/no use share.

Nominal expenditure combines prices and quantities. Dividing by the matched asset-price index gives real investment; dividing nominal spending by nominal GDP answers a different share question. Unmatched baskets can reverse a historical size inference.

Investment is a period flow, whereas a productive stock accumulates investment net of depreciation. Capital services per labour input additionally require asset weights and labour input; a spending change alone is not capital deepening.

Output per worker and output per hour differ when hours per worker change. Productivity accounting requires matched real output and labour coverage; employment counts do not supply hours or an AI counterfactual.

Unit labour cost is labour compensation divided by real output. Its change combines compensation and productivity, so it is neither hourly pay nor uniquely the result of AI; faster compensation growth can raise it despite productivity gains.

Growth-accounting contributions are weighted input-growth terms and TFP is the remaining output-growth residual. An unmatched contribution denominator or residual is not a financial return or a direct technology-treatment estimate.

Complementary intangible investment can precede measured gains, which makes delay a possible mechanism. The framework does not prove hidden benefits, rule out weak usefulness, or establish the timing or magnitude in these aggregate series.

Task substitution and complementarity can push labour demand in opposite directions; demand expansion and implementation costs affect the net result. A task mechanism is logically possible but is not a measured net employment or output effect.

Unemployment is defined relative to the labour force; employment counts, payroll jobs and population-adjusted rates differ. Changes in participation or multiple jobholding mean an aggregate rate cannot settle foregone hiring or occupation-specific losses.

Vacancies are an unfilled-position stock, while hires and separations are period flows. A fall can follow weaker demand or changed matching and does not by itself identify redundancies, AI substitution or easier recruitment.

Age or education identifies a demographic group, not task exposure. Workplace gains among existing less-experienced employees concern their task performance, not whether employers create or remove entry-level vacancies.

Advertised wages and skill requirements describe selected vacancies. Occupation, employer and applicant selection can generate premiums; AI-specific requirements and all new skills are different regressors, so the estimates are not causal training returns.

Classification and population boundaries determine which workers and output are counted. Similar labels or rebased levels do not supply a crosswalk; changes in outsourcing or composition can move averages without within-task productivity changes.

A plotted difference is descriptive unless the comparison identifies the unobserved outcome without AI. Normalisation does not remove sector-specific shocks; attribution requires an exposure design, comparison assumptions and evidence against rival trends.

Failure to see an aggregate change is not an estimated zero treatment effect. A detectable-effect claim needs a specified estimand, uncertainty and power; offsetting shocks or measurement alone do not establish a positive hidden effect either.

A public capacity listing may describe a plan or a discovered older site. Nameplate power, commissioned capacity, utilisation and energy consumed are distinct; inventory additions cannot be treated as newly completed or AI-only output.

Local grid and connection constraints can differ from national average tariffs. A price, a power rating and metered energy are different quantities, and fuel/network/contract conditions can change them without an AI-specific demand shock.

rules.pattern: \b(?:consumption band|band average|tax basis|tax treatment|semester|country mix|consumption weight|large buyer|purchas.*advantage)
rules.assessment: Price-band averages compare different customer groups with changing consumption weights, contracts and taxes. Holding thresholds fixed does not follow the same buyer, so a gap or inversion is not a causal quantity-discount estimate.

A traded input price does not reveal the quantity or expenditure share attributable to computing facilities. Other industries, supply conditions and financial demand remain uncontrolled; the series is cost context, not verified construction or an AI-demand estimate.

A published semiconductor basket and a quality-adjusted microprocessor comparison do not equal current GPU performance per dollar. Historical matched-model bias motivates checking quality methods but cannot supply a corrected present-day index.

Hosting, applications and software-development contracts purchase different services. Index rebasing only rescales a series; constant-quality cost per AI task requires a matched benchmark, product coverage and quality method.

Federal Register records publications with different document types and legal functions. Publication date is not necessarily effectiveness; keyword matches and unlinked annual flows do not establish in-force obligations, conversion cohorts, burden or international absence.

Capital expenditure is a use of funds, while operating cash flow, debt and equity are financing sources. Totals for different firms or national assets cannot be reconciled into a financing share without common scope and instruments.

A broad asset price combines expected cash flows and required returns across many firms. Without an AI-exposure universe and benchmark, it does not identify an AI valuation premium or separate expectations from discount-rate movements.

Observation date and evidence status must be preserved separately. A forecast does not become an outturn when its period begins, and unmatched or revised endpoints cannot establish a current common-window growth comparison.

Levels, proportional changes and percentage-point differences use different denominators. A comparison requires the same outcome, base and overlapping period; arithmetic consistency alone does not establish an economic mechanism.

The claim requires national industry and population definitions, not merely currency conversion. A generic productivity methodology cannot establish the exact Chinese coverage or current trend; the relevant series metadata must carry that evidence.

Purchased and own-account software are investment-account categories, not simply retained programmers' salaries. Valuation and components need separate documentation before inferring labour retention or a real-volume change.

rules.pattern: \b(?:broad uptake|rank.*benefit|size of productivity|equal AI capability|Information is not synonymous|information sector)
rules.assessment: Binary adoption and industry labels do not encode affected task shares or savings. Two industries with the same adoption rate can have different task mixes; an adoption ranking cannot imply a productivity-effect ranking.

rules.pattern: \b(?:distributional|net employment|net effect on jobs|firm.*expand|estimates have different estimands)
rules.assessment: A net employment total sums gains and losses across firms and workers. PwC surviving-firm totals and IMF local exposure estimates concern different selected units, so neither disproves heterogeneous losses or can be averaged as one treatment effect.

The IMF new-skill count is not restricted to AI, whereas PwC AI-posting comparisons use an AI skill definition. Selection and control sets differ; these are conditional advertised-wage associations, not alternative estimates of one training return.

Consumption bands contain different customers rather than following identical firms. Aggregate weights and national mixes can change the mean price, so a change between bands cannot isolate a buyer-size discount.

rules.pattern: \b(?:occupational group|occupations|definitional|how jobs are classified|Levels can differ)
rules.assessment: Occupational counts depend on survey concepts and classification membership. Two related occupation labels can cover different workers; reconciling the crosswalk is necessary before treating their level gap as substantive disagreement.

Product-basket composition and productive input mix affect the measured price or productivity aggregate. A change cannot be assigned to performance improvements or AI without matching those products and inputs.

rules.pattern: \b(?:dearer|basket definitions|service prices|these channels|useful computation|Producer price|index origin|indices.*cause|supply chain)
rules.assessment: Rebasing preserves each index's original product content. Equipment, hosting and services are different purchased outputs, so their growth gap cannot identify a common-task price or uniquely allocate energy, labour and margin effects.

A substitution decision compares total costs for equivalent useful output, including implementation, reliability and supervision. Unmatched input-price growth does not provide that comparison, and pass-through requires market-demand and supply assumptions.

rules.pattern: \b(?:One counts people|long decline before|historical benchmark|earlier.*paper|versions of a paper|own sample|age ranges|education groups)
rules.assessment: Differences in population, outcome, exposure and paper version must be kept explicit. Earlier trends are baselines, not post-treatment effects; alternative versions are revisions of evidence rather than independent bounds.

rules.pattern: \b(?:definitions.*episodes|annualised|ICT flows|structures spending|ICT is broader|infrastructure around AI|different uses and sources|rented infrastructure|investment flow)
rules.assessment: Investment accounts classify assets and measure a flow over a specified period. Structures exclude installed equipment; broad ICT includes non-AI uses, and annualised quarterly flows must not be treated as unscaled quarterly totals or a complete project budget.

rules.pattern: \b(?:current cycle is unfinished|overshoot|overoptimism|spending growth|intellectual property|local productive|European and US investment)
rules.assessment: Accounting scope and the location of recorded assets need not equal the location of productive use. This is a comparability or risk hypothesis, not a finding that a specific national difference is caused by IP relocation or that the current cycle must reverse.

Observed broad equity prices are compatible with changed expected earnings or discount rates outside AI. An exposure universe and benchmark are necessary before decomposing the movement into an AI premium.

Domestic production, imported equipment and orders cover different flows and timing. A nominal order value is not a real-volume production index; inventories and delivery lags prevent a mechanical one-to-one mapping.

rules.pattern: \b(?:first.attention|term collision|Government may|shared attention|compliance burden|three channels|logical contradiction|coincident step|common technology|prevalence needs)
rules.assessment: Publication activity and search vocabulary are not a chronology of institutional awareness or a linked cohort of substantive obligations. Shared attention, prior proposals and terminology changes provide alternatives that counts alone cannot distinguish.

National industrial averages do not observe each facility's contract, connection queue or firm supply. A local bottleneck can coexist with adequate national capacity, and a price change alone does not locate that constraint.

rules.pattern: \b(?:National accounts|historical estimates|revised|Seasonally|matching the season|Rates and counts)
rules.assessment: Release revisions, seasonal comparisons and rate denominators alter what a latest observation means. A claimed extreme requires the relevant full history and seasonal basis; metadata or an old endpoint alone cannot certify the result.

rules.pattern: \b(?:no.*treatment group|AI-specific treatment|trends.*already|long.run growth|visual change in slope|difference.*estimate|efficiency, scale)
rules.assessment: A descriptive trend or residual contains multiple influences and is not an untreated comparison. The absence of a tested break or exposure design prevents attribution of the observed aggregate difference to AI.

Recruitment incidence, success at filling vacancies and retention of existing employees are separate margins. Fewer vacancies or resilient software spending cannot establish the employment-retention mechanism without matched employer evidence.
